macros.name: addtoDirList
macros.doc: To add a new item to the end of the directory list, use \addtoDirList, the argument is the new item.

macros.name: AddToTemplate
macros.doc: Additional graphics can be overlayed with the \AddToTemplate command.

macros.name: authorColor
macros.doc: The colors of the text corresponding to \title, \author and \university on the title page can be set by using \titleColor, \authorColor and \universityColor.

macros.name: buildpanel
macros.doc: The panel overlay can be redesigned with \buildpanel, or some of the command components that make up the panel overlay can be redefined.

macros.name: ClearAllTemplates
macros.doc: The command \ClearAllTemplates is equivalent to executing \ClearTextTemplate and \ClearPanelTemplate.

macros.name: ClearBuildPanel
macros.doc: This command will clear the build panel as well as the graphics and field elements that lay on top of the panel created by the \buildpanel command.

macros.name: clearHeaders
macros.doc: The command \clearHeaders first saves the current definitions of the headers then sets the headers to the empty header.

macros.name: DeclareDocInfo
macros.doc: Information is passed through the \DeclareDocInfo command which takes a number of key-value pairs.

macros.name: DeclarePageLayout
macros.doc: The \DeclarePageLayout command gathers together many page layout parameters, both for LaTeX and for web, into one convenient package of key-value pairs.

macros.name: DesignTitlePageTrailer
macros.doc: The pro option defines the command \DesignTitlePageTrailer that takes a number of key-value pairs to describe the title page trailer.

macros.name: footerformat
macros.doc: You can set some basic formatting styles for the header and footer using \headerformat and \footerformat.

macros.name: formatPartTitle
macros.doc: The appearance of the part title can be controlled by \formatPartTitle.

macros.name: headerformat
macros.doc: You can set some basic formatting styles for the header and footer using \headerformat and \footerformat.

macros.name: headersOnSectionPage
macros.doc: Use \headersOnSectionPage to place headers on the same page as the beginning of a section.

macros.name: ifeqforpaper
macros.doc: When the forpaper option is used, the switch \ifeqforpaper is set to true.

macros.name: minPanelWidth
macros.doc: You can reset the minimal panel width using \minPanelWidth.

macros.name: navibarTextColor
macros.doc: The colors for the navigation bar can be set with commands \navibarTextColor and \navibarBgColor. Each take a single argument, a named color.

macros.name: newNaviIcon
macros.doc: The \newNaviIcon can be used to define a navigation icon.

macros.name: NewPage
macros.doc: This command expands to \newpage if the forpaper option is not taken, and does nothing, otherwise.

macros.name: noSectionNumbers
macros.doc: The command \noSectionNumbers causes web to remove the usual numbering system for a LaTeX document.

macros.name: panelNaviGroup
macros.doc: The command \panelNaviGroup can be used to create the standard navigation panel.

macros.name: panelwidth
macros.doc: To set the panel width to another value, use \panelwidth in the preamble. \panelwidth{1.25in} sets the panel width to 1.25 inches.

macros.name: prtscr
macros.doc: This command expands to print_text if the forpaper option is taken and to screen_text if not.

macros.name: restoreHeaders
macros.doc: The command \restoreHeaders restores the definitions that were in effect when the last \clearHeaders was executed.

macros.name: rfooter
macros.doc: There are convenience commands setting the running headers and footers; they are \lheader, \cheader, \rheader, \lfooter, \cfooter, and \rfooter. Each of these takes a single argument, which is the text for the header or footer in the position desired.

macros.name: rheader
macros.doc: There are convenience commands setting the running headers and footers; they are \lheader, \cheader, \rheader, \lfooter, \cfooter, and \rfooter. Each of these takes a single argument, which is the text for the header or footer in the position desired.

macros.name: screensize
macros.doc: The ⟨width⟩ and ⟨height⟩ parameters are the desired screen size of the page.

macros.name: selectColors
macros.doc: The \selectColors command can be used to set the color of most all elements of the document that have a color attribute.

macros.name: setScreensizeFromGraphic
macros.doc: If a design is not specified in the option list of web, you can use a graphic to set the screen size with \setScreensizeFromGraphic.

macros.name: titleColor
macros.doc: The colors of the text corresponding to \title, \author and \university on the title page can be set by using \titleColor, \authorColor and \universityColor.

macros.name: tocColor
macros.doc: Specifying a color through this command at any time before the creation of the table of contents will change the color of the heading.

macros.name: tocindent
macros.doc: The amount of indentation can be adjusted using \tocindent.

macros.name: tocLayout
macros.doc: The pro option also defines \tocLayout for controlling the title of the table of contents.

macros.name: topTitlePage
macros.doc: The \topTitlePage command expands to three elements: the university (affiliation), the title, and the author(s), in that order vertically.

macros.name: trailerFontSize
macros.doc: The font size of the title page trailer is set by the command \trailerFontSize, the default is \footnotesize.

macros.name: university
macros.doc: The value of \university appears on the title page.

macros.name: universityColor
macros.doc: The colors of the text corresponding to \title, \author and \university on the title page can be set by using \titleColor, \authorColor and \universityColor.

envs.name: forscreen
envs.doc: Use the forscreen environment to insert commands or content meant only for the screen.
